title: Offramp Requests & UX Sprint Scrapbook — Oct 2026
content:
Purpose

Quick, messy synthesis from the October customer-facing sprint and follow-ups. This is a working scrapbook of ‘offramp’ style asks (customers who need non-default behavior or escape hatches from the hosted defaults) + UX spike notes for the Console/product team. Not a polished decision doc — capture of signals and friction to act on in the next 2 sprints.

Topline (1-liner)

Many customers want clearer, lower-friction ways to: a) pin/fallback model variants by policy, b) manage per-route cost/latency tradeoffs in the Console, and c) get deterministic controls for function-calling + KV cache invalidation. These are high-frequency asks across mid-market and enterprise accounts.

Channels & sample sources

- Weekly CS sync (10/05) — notes + voice snippets from two enterprise trials (media analytics, legal automation)
- Field interviews (10/06–10/08) — 6 customers (mix of PLG and sales-assisted)
- Support tickets: CSREQ-487, CSREQ-503 (billing discrepancy)
- Slack: #cs-field-notes (thread 1697051200)

Concrete customer asks (ranked by frequency & urgency)

1) "Model Offramp" controls — mid-high priority
- Problem: Customers want a simple Console knob/policy to say: if a request will exceed X ms or Y tokens, route to a cheaper/faster model variant or abort with structured error.
- Why they care: unpredictable tail latency causes timeouts in their apps; they prefer predictable SLOs even if occasionally lower-quality output.
- Example quote: "We'd rather get a short, reliable answer than time out waiting for the big model." — legal automation PoC
- Quick patch idea: expose per-route latency cap + automatic fallback to pinned variant (UI: toggle + thresholds). Owner: product-hosted-api (Spike: Evelyn).

2) Per-route cost visibility + attribution — high priority
- Problem: customers struggle to map token spend to specific flows / routes in routing-heavy apps (tooling, agent calls).
- Why they care: internal chargebacks and budgeting; surprises on monthly invoices (support case CSREQ-503).
- Quick patch idea: route-level daily ledger in Console + export (CSV) and an alert for abnormal spend. Owner: billing-metrics (Spike: Tom R.).

3) Deterministic function-calling controls & reproducibility — mid priority
- Problem: function-calls behave nondeterministically across model variants; customers building workflows want reproducible invocation.
- Why: test automation and audits require deterministic outputs or at least deterministic selection of which tool/function gets invoked.
- Quick patch idea: add a per-route "function-call consistency" mode (temperature-lock + fixed-seed + model-variant pin) and a test harness example. Owner: eng-developer-ex (Jun P.).

4) KV/prefix cache invalidation & visibility — mid priority
- Problem: customers using long-running chat agents need a way to invalidate cached prefixes at route-level and see cache hit/miss rates per request.
- Why: stale context leads to hallucinations and compliance concerns with regulated data.
- Quick patch idea: Console button + API endpoint to expire cache keys for a route; surface hit/miss breakdown in trace. Owner: serving-runtime (Spike: Sofia).

5) Dedicated capacity autoscale triggers and documentation — low-medium priority but high enterprise friction
- Problem: dedicated pools sometimes scale up unexpectedly or don't scale in time for scheduled large runs. Docs are terse and onboarding triage is manual.
- Quick patch: expand the autoscale docs, add simulation tool (upload a synthetic QPS curve), and a warning banner during initial provisioning. Owner: dedicated (Docs: Maya + Infra).

Customer vignettes (short)

- Media analytics startup: heavy bursty traffic when new shows drop. They enabled default autoscale but still got a 2x invoice spike; asked for pre-commit capacity reservation UI and per-burst alerts.
- Financial firm on private: needs KV cache invalidation on policy change (KYC updates) and an audit log of which cached context was used per response.
- ML platform team: wants programmatic rollback for rollout experiments and a "safety net" automatic fallback to a tested baseline model for any canary > 10% error.

UX Spike notes (ideas / rough sketches)

1) Offramp policy canvas (Console)
- Small wizard: Select route(s) → set thresholds (latency, token count, cost) → pick fallback model/behavior (fallback model / return structured error / route to queue).
- Visualize expected cost/latency change with the policy (small histogram based on recent traffic).
- Prototype next: mock up a canvas + one-click apply to route. (Design owner: Evelyn)

2) Route ledger & anomaly detector
- Daily per-route CSV export with: requests, tokens in/out, median latency, 95p latency, fallback count, cache hit rate, errors. Add simple anomaly detector (z-score) and a muted email/pager.

3) Function-call reproducibility UX
- Toggle in route settings: "Reproducible mode" with explanatory tooltip (affects temperature/seed/variant pinning), plus a small test harness button that runs 3 deterministic samples.

Open questions / unknowns

- What model variants are compatible for safe fallback (quality degradation bounds)? Need applied-ml input to define compatibility thresholds. (Action: Spike with Applied ML — Evelyn + Jun)
- Billing-side: how do we allocate tokens for multi-tool flows where a single user request fans out? (Action: Tom to sync with Billing engineering)
- Security/compliance: cache expiry APIs — what guardrails required for Private deployments (audit log retention)? (Action: Security review requested)

Near-term next steps (this week -> next sprint)

- Product: produce low-fidelity Console mocks for Offramp policy canvas (due 10/22). Owner: Evelyn.
- Eng: prototype a simple API to expire route cache keys + surface hits (POC on branch: platform/poc/cache-expire). Owner: Sofia.
- CS: prepare 3 customer follow-ups for validation (send concept mock + 10-minute interview). Owner: Maya.

Small-risk quick wins (can be shipped as patches)

- Add a per-route CSV download (backend + minimal UI) — low effort, high signal for billing/CS teams.
- Document recommended pinning patterns for reproducible function-calling in a short runbook shared with customers.
- Add a visible banner in provisioning flow for Dedicated reminding customers about autoscale billing implications.

Notes to self / scratchpad

- Follow-up list: CSREQ-487 (latency fallback ask), CSREQ-503 (billing spike), runbook draft link, scheduled interviews (10/20–10/23).
- Slack summaries to be posted to #product-hosted-api and #infra-surge by EOD 10/19.

End.
